stem: Which of the following statements about batch mode are TRUE? (Select two.)

options.text: Classical pre-processing of the jobs runs in parallel, so a batch finishes faster than the same jobs run serially.
Jobs in a batch are not guaranteed to run in the order they were submitted, and they do not get exclusive access to the QPU.
Batch mode reserves the QPU exclusively for the duration of the batch, so no other users' jobs and no calibration jobs can be interleaved with yours.
Wrapping a single job in a batch reduces that job's queuing time compared with job mode.
Batch mode is only available on paid plans; Open Plan users cannot submit batch jobs.
A batch's maximum TTL pauses whenever another user's job occupies the QPU, so a batch never expires while some of its jobs are still queued.

explanation.correct: Batch parallelizes the classical processing of independent jobs and packs their quantum execution tightly, so a batch completes faster than serial submission. However, batched jobs are not guaranteed to run in submission order and do NOT get exclusive access — other users' jobs and calibration jobs may run in between if there is capacity.

distractors.C: Exclusive access for the whole window (no other users' jobs, no calibration jobs) is the defining feature of SESSION mode, not batch. Batch jobs share the QPU.
distractors.D: The queuing time does not decrease for the first job submitted within a batch, so batching gives no benefit for a single job.
distractors.E: It is SESSION mode that Open Plan users cannot use. Batch mode is available on the Open Plan (with a shorter maximum TTL).
distractors.F: The maximum TTL never pauses: it starts when the batch's first job starts running and runs down in wall-clock time. When it expires the batch closes — jobs already running finish, but anything still queued is failed.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — trimmed correct A, lengthened exclusivity distractor (length-tell fix). | pool wave: +F (max TTL pauses while other users run)
